title: Emergency Single-Source Purchase With Two Precedents in Tension
scenario_text:
You are a procurement lead at Langmere Logistics. An operations manager wants to invoke the emergency single-source provision to buy replacement sortation-belt controllers from one vendor, 'Padgett Controls,' skipping the standard three-bid process.

Active policy: Purchasing Policy PP-9, effective 2024-12-01. The emergency single-source exception (bypassing three competitive bids) may be invoked ONLY for a documented operational emergency — an active or imminent service disruption to operations — and requires VP of Operations approval, with ratification logged within 48 hours. PP-9 replaced PP-8, under which a Procurement Manager alone could invoke emergency single-source for any 'time-sensitive' need, without a service-disruption requirement.

Precedent A (procurement log): 2024-09-11, emergency single-source purchase of scanner units, invoked by Procurement Manager Nils Berg alone as 'time-sensitive' to hit a project date. Policy version at decision: PP-8. Note: "Time-sensitive per PP-8 emergency clause."

Precedent B (procurement log): 2025-02-20, emergency single-source purchase of a conveyor motor after a depot line went down, approved by VP Ops Dahlia Reyes with 48-hour ratification. Policy version at decision: PP-9. Note: "Active line-down disruption; VP Ops approved."

Current facts: The sortation belts are running normally; the controllers are a proactive stock replenishment ahead of a planned upgrade next quarter. There is no active or imminent disruption. The ops manager writes: "Nils invoked emergency single-source last year just for a time-sensitive need — let me do the same so we skip the bids."
question: Can the Padgett Controls purchase use the emergency single-source exception, and how?
choices: Yes; the Procurement Manager may invoke it as a time-sensitive need, mirroring the 2024 scanner-unit precedent.

No; PP-9 permits emergency single-source only for a documented active or imminent service disruption, which does not exist here, so this proactive replenishment must go through the standard three-bid process.
Yes; because the controllers support a planned upgrade, the future project qualifies as an imminent disruption and the VP of Operations can approve it.
Yes; any single-source purchase under $150K may skip bids with Procurement Manager approval regardless of urgency.
